sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- grep: Search file contents for patterns (respects .gitignore)
- find: Find files by glob pattern (respects .gitignore)
- ls: List directory contents

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

toolsAdded.name: web_fetch
toolsAdded.description:
Retrieves and extracts the main content of a web page as markdown.

Include a 'prompt' parameter to have an LLM distill the page down to just the information you need — this saves significant context compared to ingesting raw page content.
Without a prompt, the full extracted markdown is returned (or a structured overview if the page is large).

Batch mode: use 'pages' instead of 'url' to fetch multiple URLs in a single call. Each entry can have its own prompt.
This is much faster than making separate web_fetch calls when you need content from several pages.
The 'url' and 'pages' parameters are mutually exclusive. Maximum 10 pages per batch.

When to use something else:
- The gh CLI (via bash) for anything on GitHub — issues, PRs, repo contents, API calls.

Behavior notes:
- URLs must include the scheme (e.g. https://). Plain HTTP is silently upgraded to HTTPS.
- Fetched content is held in a short-lived cache, so asking multiple questions about the same page is cheap.
- Cross-host redirects are surfaced rather than followed — make a second request to the target URL.
- No files or external state are modified by this tool.

url.description: Fully-formed URL to fetch (e.g., https://example.com/page). Mutually exclusive with 'pages'.

prompt.description: What information to extract from the page. Strongly recommended — the page content will be processed by a fast LLM and only relevant information returned. Omit only if you need the full raw content. Only used with 'url', not 'pages'.
What information to extract from this page

pages.description: Array of pages to fetch concurrently (max 10). Mutually exclusive with 'url'. Each entry can have its own prompt.

# Repository Instructions

This file is the entry point for agent instructions in this repository.
Workflows and policies live in the documents under `docs/agents/`; the domain
vocabulary lives in `CONTEXT.md` at the root.

## Testing and Verification

Tests are part of the specification. Write the failing test first at the
spec's pre-agreed seams and make it green with the minimal change — red
before green, one seam, one test, one slice per cycle — per the build
discipline in [docs/agents/issue-tracker.md](docs/agents/issue-tracker.md).
Test-after is reserved for glue and wiring, UI verified by a manual test plan,
and throwaway prototypes. During implementation and review, run the focused
checks recorded under Agent skills for the changed areas and their immediate
contracts; the epic gate recorded there is reserved for the final integrated
epic commit before acceptance and closure.

## Agent skills

### Issue tracker

Gitea issues, driven by the `gitea-issues` helpers.
See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

### Triage labels

Canonical role names mapped to this tracker's label strings.
See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

### Domain docs

single layout: CONTEXT.md and ADRs live per `docs/agents/domain.md`.

### Work queue

Priority lives in the `type/roadmap` issue's ordered queue; see `docs/agents/queue.md`.

### Working standards

Docs and tests are first-class artifacts; the tracker is the queue, repository
documents the durable memory. Read the issue's epic and related issues
before planning; build test-first at the spec's pre-agreed seams; record each
change's documentation disposition and the evidence behind its merge; commands
presented as runnable must be ready to run as written. See
`docs/agents/standards.md`.

### Focused checks

`uv run --locked pytest tests/<area>`

Run on the exact current head during implementation and review follow-ups;
any later change makes this evidence stale.

### Epic gate

`make check`

The complete gate, reserved for final epic acceptance — run once on the exact
integrated commit. On an execution host, run it as
`scripts/execution_host.py gate`, which runs `make check` in a dedicated
checkout at the staged checkout's exact commit and keeps a receipt (see
`docs/runbooks/portable-execution-host.md`, "Run the gate").

# Continuous Stage A cohort

This runbook operates an `archive-stage-a-cohort/1` freeze: every block of the
reviewed archive cohort runs in schedule order from one ledger, under one
admitted configuration and one owner-approved numerical freeze
([ADR-0016](../authoritative/adr/0016-screen-stage-a-on-23-reviewed-tasks.md)).
For the release `stage-a-prepared-23-v1`, the 23 reviewed tasks with a
prepared environment each
([ADR-0029](../authoritative/adr/0029-run-agents-in-prepared-environments-keeping-declared-dependency-paths.md)),
that is 23 tasks × 7 arms = 161 slots. Approval of that freeze is the only launch decision. There is no
first-block stop, no `first_block_task_id`, no first-block audit and no owner
go/no-go between blocks.

This runbook grants no approval. It prepares the cohort on the portable
execution host (`cachyos-alexander` from attempt 7; `cachyos-asrock` before),
in the order the tools require, up to the
owner's approval of the exact freeze, then publishes, initializes and launches
it. The one-task first block keeps its own
[runbook](stage-a-first-block-gate.md).

## What the harness enforces

- **Corpus and scope.** The freeze binds the release identity, the adoption
  record's ordered task IDs and its digest. Every count (slots, attempts,
  disposition records, host preflight size) derives from the frozen corpus.
- **Per-block supervision.** `scripts/run_stage_a.py` runs at most one block
  per invocation under the unchanged per-block `SUPERVISOR_POLICY`. After a
  clean block (every slot terminal or explicitly unstarted, no reservation) it
  appends a chained record under `$artifacts/cohort-progress/` and exits `0`
  while blocks remain, or `3` when the cohort is complete. Any other result, an
  exception or a watchdog stop exits otherwise and writes no record.
- **Crash recovery.** If the process dies after a block settles but before its
  progress record is written, the next invocation writes that record from the
  ledger first (`caught_up=true`), so later blocks keep their indices. A
  completed block must be the next unrecorded block in schedule order. The
  launcher reads the ledger under its lock and fails at once if another
  launcher holds it.
- **No reset.** Each record binds the previous record and every settled slot.
  An invocation whose ledger lost or changed a settled slot, or whose record
  chain is broken, stops before any work. An active or uncertain reservation
  stops the block (`unreconciled active attempt; retain evidence, do not
  rerun`). Nothing replays, refunds or reinitializes.
- **Unattended credentials.** The unit has no terminal and never unlocks the
  vault. Every provider credential comes from the provider credential lease
  that step 2 exports with the Brave key: private files on the `/dev/shm`
  tmpfs, bound to the admitted vault's digest. A refresh-disabled ChatGPT
  token must outlive the slot's admission and native phase (4,020 s).
- **Slot rehearsal before reservation.** Before reserving each slot, the
  launcher runs that slot's native preparation up to the provider-contact
  boundary with nothing reserved: credential delivery from the lease and its
  token lifetime, Claude's token against the covering receipt, the research
  service start and stop, and the sandbox and observer definition, all torn
  down before the credential-holding Inspect evaluation would start. A failure
  stops the cohort with the slot still pending, so a resume runs it; only work
  past the boundary can leave an uncertain attempt.
- **Claude enrollment per turn.** Block entry does not require one receipt to
  cover a later Claude turn (a seventh Claude turn needs 95,400 s, more than
  a 24-hour receipt). Inside the scheduler lock, immediately before reserving
  a Claude slot, the launcher uses the latest receipt (the configured one or a
  recorded renewal) already observed and covering Claude admission plus its
  native phase (4,020 s) from the current time. Otherwise the cohort stops
  before reservation. Serial
  owner-managed dispatch (`provider_capacity_mode=owner_managed`, concurrency 1)
  makes the checked slot the one reserved.
- **Research allowance.** The freeze's numerical policy must select the
  archive research allowance `STAGE_A_ARCHIVE_ACCOUNT` (3,060 calls) or its
  top-up `STAGE_A_ARCHIVE_ACCOUNT_2`, which no other scope accepts
  ([allowance](../evidence/stage-a-archive-capacity-amendment-251-20261004.md),
  [top-up](../evidence/stage-a-archive-capacity-top-up-267-20261006.md)), and
  admission requires it to be the identity of the live allocation journal.
  Every dispatch, the launch preflight, the cohort audit and the seal require
  the live shared remainder (`identity − used − active account reservations`)
  to cover, in every dimension, one whole workflow allowance for each attempt
  of an unsettled slot that has not finished. Finished attempts are already
  charged; the lone in-flight attempt of a slot is credited with its own
  `trial-work` charges. Otherwise they stop before any reservation
  (`live research remainder cannot cover N whole workflows (<dimensions>);
  never borrow`). The check applies to every Stage A scope, so a historical
  freeze whose unsettled slots the live ledger can no longer cover is refused
  as well. Nothing borrows from another allowance.
- **Task-input store.** Archive views and verifier workspaces live in
  `${artifacts}.task-inputs`
  ([task-input retention](stage-a-first-block-gate.md#task-input-retention)).
  The cohort audit requires the store; there is no in-root fallback.
- **Unprivileged agents.** Every arm's native agent runs as the agent user
  `agent`, with the operator's UID and GID, in dispatch, research admission,
  Claude admission and image qualification alike
  ([ADR-0026](../authoritative/adr/0026-run-native-agents-as-an-unprivileged-user.md)).
  Run every command in this runbook as the unprivileged operator: the harness
  refuses to run as root. The agent owns its sanitized workspace and its arm's
  home and holds no capabilities. Inspect's sandbox-tools server stays root,
  with its state on a root-only tmpfs at `/run/sandbox-tools`, so the agent
  can neither signal it nor remove its state. Sanitization, capture, export
  and the verifier run as root. Image qualification builds each task as the
  agent and records the build's exit statuses, the user and the workspace
  handover's duration (`agent_user.handover_seconds`) in each task's record.
  `agent_user.shared_uid_accounts` and `shared_gid_groups` name any image
  account that has the operator's UID or GID; the agent still resolves to
  `agent`, ahead of them.
  An admission or image qualification made before this model does not cover
  it: re-admit and requalify at the new commit, then rebind and freeze.
- **Prepared environments.** Each task's agent works in its prepared
  environment, an owned image derived from its grader's, with its dependencies
  installed for offline use; its grader keeps the image its validator names
  ([ADR-0029](../authoritative/adr/0029-run-agents-in-prepared-environments-keeping-declared-dependency-paths.md)).
  Image preparation loads both images for the block. Sanitization keeps
  exactly the task's declared dependency paths (such as `node_modules`), each
  checked against its recorded hash, and no capture or export includes one.
  Image qualification requires the task's build to exit 0 offline as the agent
  within 600 seconds, or stops naming the task unsuitable

## Stop and resume

A failed unit (`Result` other than `success`) has stopped the cohort
fail-closed. Retain the ledger, `$artifacts`, `${artifacts}.task-inputs`, the
unit journal and image state. Diagnose the named error before anything else:

- **`unreconciled active attempt`**: an attempt was in flight or uncertain. It is
  never replayed. Reconcile it only through an existing, reviewed scheduler
  recovery with owner disposition; this runbook authorizes none.
- **`Claude enrollment cannot cover its turn`**: the next Claude slot was not
  reserved because no receipt covered it. Record a renewal (below), then
  resume. Renewing ahead of expiry avoids this stop.
- **`cohort progress chain is broken` or `scheduler ledger was reset or
  rewritten`**: the evidence changed outside the launcher. Stop and obtain an
  owner disposition; never edit records to resume.
- **`live research remainder cannot cover`**: the conserved shared account
  cannot cover the unfinished attempts' whole workflow allowances. Nothing was
  reserved. Stop; the allowance changes only by a new owner decision, never by
  borrowing or resetting usage.
- **A native sandbox failure** does not stop the cohort. Any error from the
  sandbox while the agent's process is being started or streamed is recorded
  as the slot's `infrastructure_failed` outcome, and the block continues. The
  freeze allows one attempt per slot, so that slot is terminal; it is not
  rerun. The error code is:
  - `native_process_lost` when the sandbox-tools server no longer knows the
    process. It answers `No job found with pid N`, or stops answering after a
    timed-out poll is re-polled twice. Attempt 6 showed the agent can still be
    running then: the server had been replaced, which starts a new server with
    no jobs and leaves the old server's jobs running as orphans. What replaced
    it is unconfirmed.
  - `native_sandbox_failed` for any other error, such as `exec_remote`
    failing at start or the server failing to restart.

  Before the error is recorded, a probe run with a plain `docker exec` keeps
  the server's state, then stops every process the agent started: everything
  in the container started since the job, or since the current server after a
  failed start, except pid 1 and the servers. Find both under
  `adapter.diagnostics.native_process.sandbox_failure` in the attempt's
  `native/native.json`:
  - `server_at_start` is the server and job identified when the job started.
  - `server` gives whether that server is still `alive`, the `current` one,
    whether it was `replaced`, the state directory's `entries`, and the
    bounded tail of `server-stderr.log`.
  - `stop` gives the `epoch` the agent was dated from, how many processes were
    `signalled`, any `remaining`, `confirmed`, and the `reason` when nothing
    could be signalled: no start to date the agent, or not a container.

  The outcome is recorded only once the stop is `confirmed`; Claude Code's
  driver cleanup must also confirm its own process group. An agent that
  cannot be confirmed stopped, or an outcome whose sandbox cleanup or research
  accounting cannot be confirmed, leaves the attempt uncertain and stops the
  cohort as above. `poll_timeouts` counts the timed-out polls the stream
  re-polled; the sandbox transport never re-runs a poll itself.
- **An adapter setup failure before provider contact** does not stop the
  cohort either
  ([ADR 0034](../authoritative/adr/0034-record-pre-contact-adapter-setup-failures-and-qualify-every-adapters-workspace-steps.md)).
  When an adapter records its own setup or admission failure and no tool
  inventory was approved, no provider request was forwarded. The slot
  records `infrastructure_failed` with the adapter's code, and the block
  continues; that slot is terminal. Find the code and message under
  `adapter.failure` in the attempt's `native/native.json`. Codes include:
  - `initial_workspace_unobservable`: OpenCode could not list the starting
    workspace, without its declared dependency paths, within 10 seconds and
    below Inspect's exec output limit. Image qualification checks this
    listing for every task, so it should not recur on a qualified release.
    Compare the task's `adapter_workspace.opencode` qualification record with
    the workspace in the evidence.
  - `agent_handover_failed`: the agent user could not be given the harness's
    home (Codex or OpenCode).
  - `setup_timed_out`: a Codex or OpenCode setup step outlived its own limit.
    It is not the task's wall-time timeout.
  - `setup_failed`: the sandbox failed under another setup step.
  - `harness_installation_failed`, `authentication_failed` and the other
    adapter setup codes.

  An unadmitted or changed tool inventory is not a setup failure. It still
  stops the cohort as `unadmitted native tool inventory`, or with the
  adapter's message, and the attempt is uncertain as above. So does an
  adapter failure that names no kind and code.
- **A watchdog timeout or other crash**: inspect the attempt directory and
  journal; an attempt that started is uncertain and is handled as above.
- **`private runtime research credential required` or `must be the volatile
  tmpfs lease`**: the tmpfs lease is gone, normally after a reboot. Re-export it
  ([step 2](#2-export-the-credential-leases-to-tmpfs-owner)) before
  resuming; never place the key anywhere else.

- **`TimeoutExpired` from `git fetch --no-tags origin refs/heads/main`**
  (only the older cohorts that fetch origin, see
  [above](#keep-the-host-unchanged-while-the-cohort-runs)): Gitea did not answer
  within 60 s, typically during its midnight backup. Nothing was reserved.
  Once `git -C "$checkout" ls-remote origin refs/heads/main` answers,
  `systemctl --user reset-failed "$unit"` and resume as below; after a lease
  re-export's timeout, rerun the export first.
- **`source branch moved from selected commit`** (the same cohorts, from a
  dispatch or a lease re-export): something was merged to `main`. Every later
  dispatch or export refuses the same way, so resuming cannot succeed. Retire
  the attempt (owner decision, below) and re-admit at a commit whose dispatch
  and lease re-export check the checkout locally.
- **`host admission rejected (TimeoutError)`**: before reserving, a probe hit
  its time limit: of the host (the Docker daemon, the clock, the staged
  checkout), of the archive task checkout, or of the block's task image. The
  admission phase's 300 s alarm gives the same name when it fires during these
  checks. Nothing was reserved; the slot is still pending. A cohort admitted
  at an older commit shows a raw `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` from these probes
  instead: from `git fetch`, follow the entry above; from any other probe,
  this one. From `$checkout`, check the services the probes use:

  ```sh
  .venv/bin/python -B scripts/execution_host.py doctor --json \
    | .venv/bin/python -B -c 'import json,sys; c={c["name"]: c for c in json.load(sys.stdin)["checks"]}; [print(n, c[n]["status"], c[n]["detail"]) for n in ("daemon", "ntp", "checkout")]'
  timeout 30 git -C "$archive_root" status --porcelain --untracked-files=no && echo 'archive checkout answers'
  ```

  Expected: three lines beginning `daemon PASS`, `ntp PASS` and
  `checkout PASS`, then `archive checkout answers` with nothing before it.
  Doctor reports an unreachable daemon or an unsynchronized clock as
  `OWNER-STEP`, not `FAIL`; a daemon that still hangs shows as
  `daemon OWNER-STEP … unreachable: no response within 60 s`. (Doctor in a
  checkout admitted before it reported this crashes with `TimeoutExpired`
  instead, and the snippet reports a JSON error; it means the same.) Wait and
  rerun until everything passes, then `systemctl --user reset-failed "$unit"`
  and resume as below. A probe that hangs again is a host fault: diagnose it,
  do not resume in a loop.

- **A slot rehearsal failure** (for example `provider credential lease is
  missing`, `Codex ChatGPT access token expires before the pilot's worst-case
  attempt window`, `fresh Max 5x evaluation-only enrollment evidence
  required`, or a research service or sandbox error): the slot is still
  pending and nothing was reserved. Fix the cause (re-export the leases after
  a reboot, record a Claude renewal), then resume. An expired ChatGPT token
  needs a new login, which changes the vault the host was admitted with:
  retire the attempt and re-admit.

Resuming is a recovery, not a new approval. It must use the same freeze,
configuration, ledger, admission, approval, host profile and artifact root,
and it starts the same unit command above. A failed transient unit stays
loaded and `systemd-run` refuses its name: clear it first with
`systemctl --user reset-failed "$unit"`, then run the [launch](#launch) blocks. Each invocation re-authenticates
every input and the progress chain before it reserves anything; a changed
configuration or ledger is rejected. Never delete, reset or reinitialize the
ledger, and never move the artifact root of an attempt that will resume.
After any reboot, re-export the leases (step 2) before the resumed unit starts.

When the cohort is stopped for good (an owner decision not to resume), remove
the leases so the keys leave the host's memory:

```sh
providers="$(dirname "$lease")/stage-a-provider-credentials"
rm -- "$lease" "$providers"/* && rmdir -- "$providers" "$(dirname "$lease")" && echo 'credential leases removed'
```

### Retire a stopped attempt (owner decision)

An attempt whose launched cohort stopped with an uncertain reservation cannot
resume, and a new attempt needs a new freeze and an empty ledger at the
admitted path. With the owner's recorded decision to start a new attempt (for
example after a code fix that needs re-admission), retire the stopped attempt

in [Paths and shell](#paths-and-shell), from its still-admitted staged

# Stage-aware benchmark scheduler

Issue #23 supplies the persistent scheduling and reservation boundary shared by
Stage A and Stage B. It does not launch an agent, authorize a synthetic manifest,
or seal benchmark outcomes; issue #24 owns those operations.

## Frozen inputs

Initialize a ledger only from the exact owner-approved `purpose=freeze` v5
manifest reconciled by issue #165 from issue #50's validated corpus. The
scheduler accepts only the current v5 contract. Recover historical ledgers at
their recorded implementation revisions. The whole canonical manifest digest is the resume identity. The
scheduler rejects changes to the stage, corpus, arm set, schedule, source policy,
resources, outcome contract, or any other frozen field.

A v5 Stage A task/repetition block contains exactly the seven canonical standard
arms, including `claude-code-claude-opus-5`. A v5 Stage B block contains zero
through seven survivors derived from its content-addressed 175-slot Stage A
capability disposition, followed by both RelayView arms and standard Pi, for
three through ten slots. The disposition must bind the exact Stage A freeze and
slot plan; the manifest's deterministic seeded order and outcome slot plan must
also agree exactly before a ledger is created.

```sh
python scripts/stage_scheduler.py init path/to/stage-a-freeze.json logs/local/stage-a/scheduler.json
```

Synthetic contract fixtures require the explicit `--allow-fixture` flag and
remain incapable of authorizing a live cohort. Supply that flag on every
fixture mutation (`init`, `next`, `finish`, and `reconcile`); fixture leases are
also returned with `manifest_purpose=fixture` and `simulation=true`. Production
runners must accept only `manifest_purpose=freeze` and `simulation=false`.

Every Stage B operation additionally authenticates the sealed Stage A manifest:

```sh
python scripts/stage_scheduler.py init path/to/stage-b-freeze.json logs/local/stage-b/scheduler.json \
  --stage-a-freeze path/to/sealed-stage-a-freeze.json \
  --trusted-stage-a-freeze-digest sha256:aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa \
  --trusted-stage-a-disposition-digest sha256:bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb \
  --trusted-stage-a-outcome-seal-digest sha256:cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc
```

Supply the same four trust arguments to `status`, `next`, `finish`, and
`reconcile`. The scheduler persists the trusted digests and rejects a missing
or different value on resume.

## Owner-managed Stage A capacity

Stage A numerical policy v2 records `provider_capacity_mode=owner_managed`.
The owner verifies sufficient provider and Brave capacity outside the runner;
neither the launcher nor scheduler accepts quota observations for that cohort.
The scheduler still serializes each declared account, atomically retains every
whole-workflow reservation and consumption, enforces local and account
parallelism, and preserves typed provider/rate-limit failures. Per-trial token
usage remains provider-reported execution evidence, not scheduler capacity
telemetry.

## Legacy and Stage B quota observations

For a freeze that retains an observation-based capacity policy, provide a JSON
array before each selection with exactly one current observation
for every account that may be used by the next slot. Never include a credential,
token, prompt, response body, or provider payload. A safe observation has this
shape:

```json
[
  {
    "account_id": "openai-frozen-account-id",
    "observed_at": "2026-09-12T13:00:00Z",
    "valid_until": "2026-09-12T13:05:00Z",
    "remaining_workflows": 12,
    "weekly_remaining_workflows": 20,
    "conservative_capacity_workflows": null,
    "recovery_at": "2026-09-12T17:00:00Z",
    "weekly_recovery_at": "2026-09-17T00:00:00Z",
    "external_usage_workflows": 0,
    "evidence_digest": "sha256:aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"
  }
]
```

`null` remaining values never mean unlimited. An account frozen with `pause`
stays blocked. An account frozen with `conservative_reservation` also needs an
explicit `conservative_capacity_workflows` value. The scheduler subtracts the
observed external usage, frozen external-use percentage, safety workflows,
completed consumption since the observation, and active whole-workflow
reservations. Rolling and weekly recovery times remain distinct in retained
evidence. If only one remaining value is unknown, conservative capacity fills
only that unknown value; it never replaces a known exhausted limit. Every
blocked decision retains the safe quota observations that supported it and the
dispatch or wait event links back to those deferrals by stable decision
identity. Resume replays each decision against the observations, historical
reservations, parallelism, pending attempt, and event order.

Reserve the next eligible slot atomically:

```sh
python scripts/stage_scheduler.py next path/to/stage-a-freeze.json logs/local/stage-a/scheduler.json
```

For a legacy observation-based policy, append
`path/to/quota-observations.json`. Omitting that file for a legacy policy or
supplying it for an owner-managed Stage A policy fails closed.

The returned lease binds the manifest, stable slot/trial/attempt IDs, arm, task,
repetition, and all account reservations. Pass that identity unchanged to #24's
runner. The scheduler may defer a blocked arm and select a later arm only within
the same seeded task/repetition block. It never begins the next block while the
current one is open.

## Attempt completion

Record exactly one typed outcome and retained evidence digest for the active
lease:

```sh
python scripts/stage_scheduler.py finish path/to/stage-a-freeze.json logs/local/stage-a/scheduler.json \
  --lease 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 \
  --outcome result_recorded \
  --evidence-digest sha256:aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
```

`result_recorded` binds the complete #24/#131 outcome evidence without asking the
scheduler to reinterpret verifier, termination, delivery, or primary-score
dimensions. Every `infrastructure_failed` outcome requires a nonempty typed
error code. The current v5 policy permits one attempt per slot and no automatic
retry. Incorrect patches, eligible timeouts, unsupported tasks and infrastructure
failures retain their terminal disposition; an ambiguous in-flight attempt requires
explicit evidence reconciliation and cannot be replayed automatically.

Inspect a resumable ledger at any time:

```sh
python scripts/stage_scheduler.py status path/to/stage-a-freeze.json logs/local/stage-a/scheduler.json
```

## Finite stop and reconciliation

Quota waiting is recorded separately from attempt runtime. After the frozen
cohort end, stop dispatch, ensure no attempt remains in flight, and reconcile
every pending slot as unstarted with retained stop evidence:

```sh
python scripts/stage_scheduler.py reconcile path/to/stage-a-freeze.json logs/local/stage-a/scheduler.json \
  --reason "finite cohort window elapsed" \
  --evidence-digest sha256:aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
```

def run_block(freeze, configuration, *, ledger, admission_directory, approval_path,
              trusted_host_digest, host_profile, output, execute, rehearse=None,
              continuation=None, first_block_audit=None):
    """Execute at most the current task block; `execute` is the native worker.

    Before each reservation, `rehearse` runs the next slot's native
    preparation up to the provider-contact boundary with nothing reserved:
    credential delivery, token lifetime, the research service and the sandbox
    definition. A rehearsal failure stops the block while the slot is still
    pending, so resuming runs it; only work past the boundary can leave an
    uncertain attempt.

    Injecting a worker is an internal test seam. The executable CLI supplies the
    pinned native/independent-verifier worker and its rehearsal, never an
    owner-supplied command.
    """
    from agent_harness_evals.stage_a_execution import EXECUTION_POLICY, phase_deadline
    with phase_deadline(EXECUTION_POLICY['block_setup_seconds']/2, 'block inputs'):
        ledger, output = Path(ledger), Path(output)
        approval = read(Path(approval_path))
        target = read(Path(admission_directory)/'target-admission.json')
        verify_plan(freeze, configuration, approval, target)
        verify_configured_freeze(freeze, configuration)
        verify_execution_inputs(configuration, admission_directory)
        # The original receipt was just authenticated against admission; per-turn checks pin it.
        frozen_enrollment_digest = digest(read(Path(configuration['claude_enrollment'])))
        require(output.is_absolute() and output.resolve()==output, 'canonical artifact directory required')
        output.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        host = HostAdmission(Path(host_profile), trusted_host_digest, ledger)
        verify_admitted_locations(configuration, read(Path(host_profile)),
                                  read(Path(admission_directory)/'allocation-receipt.json'),
                                  ledger=ledger, output=output)
        admission = StageAAdmission(Path(admission_directory), Path(approval_path))
        store = TaskImageStore(ledger)
    with lock(ledger.with_name('.stage-a-launcher.lock')):
        with phase_deadline(EXECUTION_POLICY['block_setup_seconds']/2, 'block state'):
            state = load_state(ledger, freeze)
            require(not state['reservations'], 'unreconciled active attempt; retain evidence, do not rerun')
            check_block_gate(state, freeze, continuation, first_block_audit,
                             first_block_task_id=configuration.get('first_block_task_id'))
            verify_pending_enrollment(state, configuration, at=now(), cohort=is_cohort(freeze))
            block = _current_block(state)
            if not block:
                return {'status':'complete', 'new_attempts':0}
            task_id = block[0]['task_id']
            if freeze.get('execution_scope') is not None:
                selected, row = export_block_inputs(freeze, configuration, task_id, output)
            else:
                selected, row = load_block_task(freeze, configuration, task_id)
            prior = store.state() if store.path.exists() else None
            if prior and prior['status']!='released' and prior['task_id']!=task_id:
                # load_state proved that there is no lease for the old block.
                require(not any(s['task_id']==prior['task_id'] and s['status']!='terminal' for s in state['slots']),
                        'previous image still belongs to an unfinished block')
                store.release()
        image = configuration['images'][task_id]
        with phase_deadline(EXECUTION_POLICY['image_preparation_seconds'], 'image preparation'):
            store.prepare(selected, expanded_upper_bytes=image['expanded_upper_bytes'], archive=image.get('archive'),
                          agent_expanded_upper_bytes=image.get('agent_expanded_upper_bytes'))
        completed = []
        while True:
            if rehearse is not None:
                upcoming = next((slot for slot in _current_block(load_state(ledger, freeze))
                                 if slot['status'] == 'pending' and slot['task_id'] == task_id), None)
                if upcoming is not None:
                    # Serial owner-managed dispatch reserves exactly this first pending slot.
                    rehearse(selected, row, next(a for a in freeze['arms'] if a['arm_id'] == upcoming['arm_id']),
                             freeze, configuration)
            with phase_deadline(EXECUTION_POLICY['admission_seconds'], 'admission'):
                from agent_harness_evals.stage_a_execution import retained_input
                for settings in configuration['arms'].values():
                    retained_input(settings['research_setup'])
                    retained_input(settings['admission_profile'])
                with locked_state(ledger, freeze) as state:
                    block = _current_block(state)
                    if not block or block[0]['task_id']!=task_id:
                        break
                    coverage = None
                    if is_cohort(freeze):
                        from agent_harness_evals.stage_a_enrollment import verify_claude_turn
                        # Fails closed before reservation when Claude's turn is uncovered.
                        coverage = verify_claude_turn(state, configuration, output,
                                                      frozen_enrollment_digest, at=now())
                    lease = dispatch_next(state, freeze, observations=None,
                                          claude_reading=None, now=now(),
                                          host_admission=host, stage_a_admission=admission)
                attempt = output/lease['lease_id']
                require(not attempt.exists(), 'attempt artifacts already exist; do not replay')
                attempt.mkdir(mode=0o700)
                intent = {'schema_version':'stage-a-launch-intent/1', 'lease':lease,
                          'configuration_digest':digest(configuration), 'started_at':now()}
                if coverage is not None:
                    intent['enrollment_coverage'] = coverage
                write(attempt/'intent.json', intent)
            try:
                arm = next(a for a in freeze['arms'] if a['arm_id']==lease['arm_id'])
                outcome = execute(
                    selected, row, arm, lease, freeze, configuration, attempt, store
                )
                with phase_deadline(EXECUTION_POLICY['recording_seconds'], 'recording'):
                    require(outcome['lease_id']==lease['lease_id'] and outcome['cleanup_confirmed'] is True,
                            'worker outcome or cleanup is incomplete')
                    write(attempt/'completion.json', outcome)
                    with locked_state(ledger, freeze) as state:
                        record_attempt(state, freeze, lease_id=lease['lease_id'], outcome=outcome['outcome'],
                                       error_code=outcome.get('error_code'), evidence_digest=digest(outcome), finished_at=now())
                        remaining = _current_block(state)
                        block_complete = not remaining or remaining[0]['task_id'] != task_id
                    completed.append(lease['lease_id'])
                if block_complete:
                    break
            except BaseException as error:
                write(attempt/'interrupted.json', {'lease_id':lease['lease_id'], 'error_type':type(error).__name__,
                                                  'at':now(), 'automatic_retry':False, 'charges_refunded':False})
                raise
        with phase_deadline(EXECUTION_POLICY['image_cleanup_seconds'], 'image cleanup'):
            store.release()
        return {'status':'block_complete', 'task_id':task_id, 'attempts':completed,
                'first_block_gate':not is_cohort(freeze) and task_id==freeze['schedule'][0]['task_id']}


PROGRESS_SCHEMA = 'stage-a-cohort-progress/1'
PROGRESS_DIR = 'cohort-progress'


def _blocks(state):
    """Block task IDs in schedule order; the ledger keeps its slots in the frozen order."""
    return list(dict.fromkeys(slot['task_id'] for slot in state['slots']))


def _verify_progress(freeze, state, progress):
    """Prove the clean-block chain, its schedule order, and that the ledger only grew since."""
    records = sorted(progress.glob('block-*.json')) if progress.exists() else []
    blocks = _blocks(state)
    previous = None
    for index, path in enumerate(records, 1):
        record = read(path)
        require(path.name == f'block-{index:04d}.json' and record.get('schema_version') == PROGRESS_SCHEMA
                and record.get('index') == index and record.get('manifest_digest') == digest(freeze)
                and index <= len(blocks) and record.get('task_id') == blocks[index - 1]
                and record.get('previous_digest') == (None if previous is None else digest(previous)),
                'cohort progress chain is broken')
        previous = record
    if previous is not None:
        slots = {slot['slot_id']: slot for slot in state['slots']}
        require(digest([slots.get(slot_id) for slot_id in previous['settled_slot_ids']])
                == previous['settled_slots_digest'],
                'scheduler ledger was reset or rewritten since the last clean block')
    return previous


def _record_block(freeze, state, task_id, previous, output, *, caught_up):
    """Append the next chained progress record for a settled block, with no reservation open."""
    block = [slot for slot in state['slots'] if slot['task_id'] == task_id]
    require(block and all(slot['status'] in SETTLED for slot in block) and not state['reservations'],
            'block did not complete cleanly; the cohort stops without advancing')
    settled = [slot for slot in state['slots'] if slot['status'] in SETTLED]
    index = 1 if previous is None else previous['index'] + 1
    record = {'schema_version': PROGRESS_SCHEMA, 'index': index, 'task_id': task_id,
              'manifest_digest': digest(freeze),
              'previous_digest': None if previous is None else digest(previous),
              'settled_slot_ids': [slot['slot_id'] for slot in settled],
              'settled_slots_digest': digest(settled), 'caught_up': caught_up,
              'renewal_digests': [digest(read(path)) for path in sorted(
                  (output / 'enrollment-renewals').glob('renewal-*.json'))],
              'recorded_at': now()}
    progress = output / PROGRESS_DIR
    progress.mkdir(mode=0o700, exist_ok=True)
    path = progress / f'block-{index:04d}.json'
    require(not path.exists(), 'cohort progress record already exists')
    write(path, record)
    return record, path


def _checked_ledger(freeze, ledger, output):
    """Under the launcher lock: the exact ledger, its progress chain, and any record a crash left unwritten.

    If the process died after a block settled but before its record was written,
    that record is written now from the ledger, with the same checks, so later
    blocks keep their indices. Returns the last record and the next unrecorded block.
    """
    state = read(ledger)
    require(state.get('manifest_digest') == digest(freeze), 'scheduler ledger belongs to another freeze')
    previous = _verify_progress(freeze, state, output / PROGRESS_DIR)
    blocks = _blocks(state)
    while True:
        recorded = 0 if previous is None else previous['index']
        if recorded == len(blocks):
            return state, previous, None
        pending = blocks[recorded]
        if any(slot['status'] not in SETTLED for slot in state['slots'] if slot['task_id'] == pending):
            return state, previous, pending
        previous, _ = _record_block(freeze, state, pending, previous, output, caught_up=True)


def run_cohort_step(freeze, *, ledger, output, run):
    """One supervised invocation of a continuous full cohort (ADR-0016).

    `run` executes at most the current block (the bound `run_block`). A clean
    block that is the next unrecorded block in schedule order appends a chained
    progress record and returns `advance`, or `complete` when no slot remains
    pending; the supervisor then restarts the same command for the next block.
    Anything else raises and stops the cohort. The ledger is read under the
    launcher lock and never reset: a settled slot that changed since the last
    record stops the run before any work.
    """
    require(is_cohort(freeze), 'continuous advance requires the full-cohort scope')
    ledger, output = Path(ledger), Path(output)
    launcher_lock = ledger.with_name('.stage-a-launcher.lock')
    with lock(launcher_lock):  # fails at once while another launcher runs a block
        _, _, expected = _checked_ledger(freeze, ledger, output)
    result = run()
    with lock(launcher_lock):
        state = read(ledger)
        previous = _verify_progress(freeze, state, output / PROGRESS_DIR)
        if result.get('status') == 'complete':
            require(expected is None and not state['reservations']
                    and all(slot['status'] in SETTLED for slot in state['slots']),
                    'cohort reported complete with unsettled slots or reservations')
            return {'decision': 'complete', 'result': result}
        require(result.get('status') == 'block_complete' and result.get('task_id') == expected,
                'block did not complete in schedule order; the cohort stops without advancing')
        record, path = _record_block(freeze, state, expected, previous, output, caught_up=False)
        remaining = any(slot['status'] not in SETTLED for slot in state['slots'])
        return {'decision': 'advance' if remaining else 'complete', 'progress': str(path), 'result': result}

"""Native execution and independent outcome normalization for reserved Stage A slots."""
from contextlib import contextmanager
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
import hashlib
from pathlib import Path
import signal
import uuid
from urllib.parse import urlparse

from agent_harness_evals.research_contract import digest
from agent_harness_evals.multilang_test_overlay import POLICY as TEST_COMPOSITION_POLICY
from agent_harness_evals.stage_a_storage import read, require, write
from agent_harness_evals.security import redact_for_persistence
from agent_harness_evals.stage_a_task import WORKFLOW_SECONDS
from agent_harness_evals.task_outcomes_v2 import (
    derive_task_outcome, normalized_benchmark_result_v2, _receipt_observations)

# Includes workspace preparation, native execution, candidate capture and
# container startup. Hidden verification has its own 7200-second deadline.
NATIVE_PHASE_SECONDS = 3720
# Inspect 0.3.261: compose down and config --images each allow 300 seconds,
# then retries of 60 and 30. Three sequential, prebuilt-image evaluations
# reserve 3 * 2 * 390 seconds, plus 180 for credential/service cleanup.
# These are allowances; the admitted systemd block watchdog is the hard bound.
EXECUTION_POLICY = {
    'backend': 'inspect-sequential-v1',
    'test_composition': {
        'policy': TEST_COMPOSITION_POLICY,
        'implementation_sha256': hashlib.sha256(Path(__file__).with_name('multilang_test_overlay.py').read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
    },
    'native_phase_seconds': NATIVE_PHASE_SECONDS, 'workflow_seconds': WORKFLOW_SECONDS,
    'verifier_seconds':7200, 'cleanup_reserve_seconds':2520,
    'image_preparation_seconds':7200, 'image_cleanup_seconds':120, 'arms_per_image':7,
    # Successor source/lifecycle authentication alone measured 118.238 seconds
    # under the admitted 1-CPU controller. Include the remaining admission
    # checks and headroom without weakening them or extending native work.
    'block_setup_seconds':300, 'admission_seconds':300,
    'normalization_seconds':120, 'recording_seconds':120,
    'per_attempt_overhead_seconds':13269,
}


def block_budget_seconds():
    p = EXECUTION_POLICY
    return (p['block_setup_seconds'] + p['image_preparation_seconds'] + p['image_cleanup_seconds'] +
            p['arms_per_image'] * sum(p[key] for key in (
                'native_phase_seconds', 'verifier_seconds', 'cleanup_reserve_seconds',
                'admission_seconds', 'normalization_seconds', 'recording_seconds')))


# The provider-free qualification service has a short preparation watchdog. A
# comparative block needs its own frozen controller cgroup and a small margin
# around the sum of every enforced phase deadline. Docker sandboxes retain their
# separately admitted 28-GiB/16-CPU limits.
SUPERVISOR_POLICY = {
    'schema_version': 'stage-a-block-supervisor/1',
    'cpu_percent': 100,
    'memory_bytes': 2 * 1024 ** 3,
    'tasks': 128,
    'runtime_seconds': block_budget_seconds() + 300,
}


# A refresh-disabled access token must outlive the attempt's admission and native phase.
CREDENTIAL_LIFETIME_SECONDS = EXECUTION_POLICY['admission_seconds'] + NATIVE_PHASE_SECONDS
# A slot's rehearsal precedes its live credential check by at most the
# rehearsal-inputs, native-preparation and native-inputs bounds (60 s each)
# and the admission phase, so a token that passes the rehearsal passes then too.
REHEARSAL_MARGIN_SECONDS = EXECUTION_POLICY['admission_seconds'] + 3 * 60


def native_credential(arm_id, configuration, *, margin_seconds=0):
    """The arm's provider and its source in the provider credential lease, bound to this vault.

    The supervised cohort has no terminal and never unlocks the vault; the
    owner exports the lease once per boot (`export_stage_a_research_lease.py`).
    """
    from agent_harness_evals.local_runner import _keepassxc_database_identity
    from agent_harness_evals.stage_a_provider_credentials import credential
    pin = _keepassxc_database_identity(Path(configuration['database']))[0]
    return credential(arm_id, database_sha256=pin,
                      minimum_access_ttl_seconds=CREDENTIAL_LIFETIME_SECONDS + margin_seconds)


def native_inputs(arm_id, configuration):
    """The arm's retained research setup, with a fresh deadline, and its admission profile."""
    from agent_harness_evals.research_budget import require_budget
    settings = configuration['arms'][arm_id]
    setup = retained_input(settings['research_setup'])
    require_budget(setup)
    # This creates a new workflow identity in the same conserved account epoch.
    setup['deadlineMs'] = int(datetime.now(timezone.utc).timestamp()*1000) + NATIVE_PHASE_SECONDS*1000
    return setup, retained_input(settings['admission_profile'])


def retained_input(reference):
    path = Path(reference['path'])
    require(path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink() and path.stat().st_size <= 16*1024**2,
            'unsafe launcher input')
    require(hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()==reference['sha256'], 'launcher input changed')
    return read(path)


def utcnow():
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


@contextmanager
def phase_deadline(seconds, label):
    """Bound synchronous controller work; never surround an Inspect evaluation."""
    require(seconds > 0, 'positive phase allowance required')
    def expired(signum, frame):
        raise TimeoutError(label + ' phase exceeded its frozen wall-clock bound')
    previous = signal.getsignal(signal.SIGALRM)
    require(signal.getitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL)==(0.0,0.0), 'another process deadline is active')
    signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, expired)
    signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, seconds)
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, 0)
        signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, previous)


def terminal_reason(adapter):
    if adapter.get('termination_reason'):
        return adapter['termination_reason']
    failure = adapter.get('failure') or {}
    if failure.get('code')=='task_timeout':
        return 'deadline_timeout'
    if failure.get('kind') in {'authentication','admission'}:
        return 'authentication_failure' if failure['kind']=='authentication' else 'setup_failure'
    if failure:
        return 'provider_failure' if failure.get('kind')=='provider' else 'infrastructure_failure'
    return 'completed' if adapter.get('terminal',{}).get('state')=='completed' else 'unknown'


def normalized_usage(harness, usage):
    """Common token totals; provider-specific buckets stay in native evidence."""
    fields = ('input_tokens','output_tokens','provider_reported','unavailable_fields')
    if harness != 'claude-code':
        return {key:usage[key] for key in fields}
    inputs = [usage.get(key) for key in ('input_tokens','cache_creation_input_tokens','cache_read_input_tokens')]
    total = sum(inputs) if all(type(value) is int and value>=0 for value in inputs) else None
    output = usage.get('output_tokens')
    output = output if type(output) is int and output>=0 else None
    values = {'input_tokens':total,'output_tokens':output}
    return {**values,'provider_reported':any(value is not None for value in values.values()),
            'unavailable_fields':[key for key,value in values.items() if value is None]}


def normalize(freeze, arm, lease, native, verifier, verification_started_at, output, *, persist=True):
    """Retain lifecycle facts and apply the existing v2 outcome contract."""
    from agent_harness_evals.stage_a_native import recorded_failure_code
    output = Path(output)
    def retain(path, value):
        if persist:
            write(path,value)
        else:
            require(read(path)==value, 'retained normalization evidence differs')
    adapter = native['adapter']
    role = arm['roles'][0]
    slot = next(s for s in freeze['outcome_slot_plan']['slots'] if s['slot_id']==lease['slot_id'])
    terminal = {'result_id':str(uuid.uuid5(uuid.UUID(lease['lease_id']), 'stage-a-result')),
                'trial_id':lease['trial_id'], 'slot_id':lease['slot_id'], 'arm_id':arm['arm_id'],
                'manifest_digest':slot['manifest_digest'], 'task':slot['task'], 'attempt':lease['attempt'],
                'terminal':True}
    timing = adapter['timing']
    started = datetime.fromisoformat(timing['started_at'])
    deadline = (started+timedelta(seconds=WORKFLOW_SECONDS)).isoformat()
    reason = terminal_reason(adapter)
    # A sandbox or setup failure can come before the agent's first provider request.
    if (native.get('authentication_confirmed') is not True and
            not recorded_failure_code(adapter, inventories=native.get('inventory_digests'))):
        reason = 'authentication_failure'
    candidate = native['candidate']
    candidate_path = 'candidate.json' if candidate['status']=='exported' else None
    if candidate_path:
        # Redacted like every persisted copy; `sha256` and `bytes` still name the exact patch graded,
        # which an archive grade keeps in the task-input store (ADR 0024).
        retain(output/candidate_path, redact_for_persistence(candidate))
    # The verifier result remains independent of timeout/primary scoring.
    value = verifier.get('resolved')
    score = int(value) if type(value) is bool else None
    unavailable = verifier.get('unavailable_reason', 'verifier_result_unavailable') if score is None else None
    retain(output/'verifier.json', verifier)
    accepted = adapter.get('admission',{}).get('status')=='accepted'
    activity = native.get('agent_activity_observed') is True
    receipt = {'schema_version':'task-outcome-evidence-1.0', 'terminal_record':terminal, 'events':{
        'authentication':'succeeded' if native.get('authentication_confirmed') is True else 'unavailable',
        'admission':'succeeded' if accepted else 'failed',
        'workspace':'ready' if native['repository_sanitization']['validated'] else 'failed',
        'agent_activity':'observed' if activity else 'not_observed', 'termination_reason':reason,
        'frozen_deadline_at':deadline, 'deadline_event_at':deadline if reason=='deadline_timeout' else None,
        'automatic_work_stopped_at':native['automatic_work_stopped_at'],
        'candidate':{'artifact':candidate_path,
                     'exported_at':native['candidate_exported_at'] if candidate_path else None,
                     'unavailable_reason':candidate.get('unavailable_reason')},
        'verification':{'started_at':verification_started_at, 'score':score,
                        'report_artifact':'verifier.json', 'unavailable_reason':unavailable},
        'feedback_events':[], 'automated_disposition':{'applicable':False,'status':'not_applicable'},
        'human_disposition':{'applicable':False,'status':'not_applicable'}}}
    retain(output/'lifecycle.json', receipt)
    observed = _receipt_observations(receipt)
    evidence = ['lifecycle.json']
    dimensions = derive_task_outcome(
        verifier_status=observed['verifier_result']['status'], terminal_reason=reason,
        delivery_status=observed['delivery']['status'], eligibility=observed['timeout_eligibility'],
        verifier_evidence=evidence, termination_evidence=evidence, delivery_evidence=evidence,
        eligibility_evidence=evidence, evaluator_integrity_evidence=evidence,
        evaluator_integrity=observed['evaluator_integrity'], report_artifact='verifier.json',
        candidate_artifact=candidate_path, verifier_unavailable_reason=unavailable,
        delivery_unavailable_reason=candidate.get('unavailable_reason'))
    paths = ['native/native.json','native/inspect.json','native/transport.json','verifier.json','lifecycle.json']
    paths.extend(str(p.relative_to(output)) for p in sorted(output.rglob('inspect*.json*'))
                 if str(p.relative_to(output)) not in paths)
    if (output/'native/research.json').is_file():
        paths.append('native/research.json')
    if candidate_path:
        paths.append(candidate_path)
    archive_tasks = [task for task in freeze.get('corpus',{}).get('tasks',[])
                     if task['task_id']==slot['task']['id'] and 'archive_binding' in task]
    require(len(archive_tasks)<=1, 'ambiguous archive result identity')
    if archive_tasks:
        binding = archive_tasks[0]['archive_binding']
        retain(output/'archive-binding.json', binding)
        paths.append('archive-binding.json')
        if score is not None:
            require((output/'grade.json').is_file() and (output/'test.log').is_file(),
                    'archive grade evidence is missing')

    freeze: Mapping[str, Any],

    lease_id: str,

    lease = intent.get("lease", {})
    expected = {"lease_id": lease_id, "trial_id": state_slot["trial_id"],

            completion.get("lease_id") == lease_id and completion.get("cleanup_confirmed") is True and
            completion.get("outcome") == attempt["outcome"] and
            completion.get("error_code") == attempt.get("error_code") and
            digest(completion) == attempt["evidence_digest"] == state_slot["terminal"]["evidence_digest"],
            "scheduler disposition differs from retained completion evidence")
    result_path = Path(completion.get("result_path", ""))
    require(result_path.is_absolute() and result_path.resolve() == attempt_root / "result.json" and
            completion.get("result_digest") == digest(result),
            "completion result identity or path changed")
    result_identity = {key: expected[key] for key in ("trial_id", "slot_id", "arm_id", "attempt")}
    planned = next(plan for plan in freeze["outcome_slot_plan"]["slots"]
                   if plan["slot_id"] == state_slot["slot_id"])
    result_identity.update(manifest_digest=planned["manifest_digest"], task=planned["task"])
    require(all(result.get(key) == value for key, value in result_identity.items()),

    validate_normalized_benchmark_result_v2(result, artifact_root=attempt_root)
    events = lifecycle["events"]
    integrity = result["outcome_dimensions"]["evaluator_integrity"]
    require(events["feedback_events"] == [] and
            integrity["automatic_work_quiescent_before_verification"] is True and
            integrity["hidden_feedback_returned_to_agent"] is False and
            integrity["hidden_feedback_used_for_retry_or_selection"] is False,
            "hidden score isolation or evaluator quiescence failed")
    row = {"slot_id": state_slot["slot_id"], "trial_id": state_slot["trial_id"],
            "attempt_id": attempt["attempt_id"], "lease_id": lease_id,
            "task_id": state_slot["task_id"], "repetition": state_slot["repetition"],
            "arm_id": state_slot["arm_id"], "planned_order": state_slot["planned_order"],

DECISION_SCHEMA = "stage-a-continuation-approval/2"
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
AUDIT_NAME = "first-block-audit.json"
DECISION_NAME = "first-block-decision.json"


def _first_schedule_block(freeze: Mapping) -> list[Mapping]:
    require(freeze.get("purpose") == "freeze" and freeze.get("stage") == "stage_a",
            "first-block audit requires the final purpose=freeze Stage A manifest")
    require(freeze.get("schema_version") == "staged-multilang-benchmark/5" and
            len(freeze.get("arms", [])) == 7,
            "first-block audit requires the current seven-arm v5 contract")
    schedule = freeze.get("schedule")
    require(isinstance(schedule, list) and schedule, "frozen schedule is empty")
    identity = (schedule[0]["task_id"], schedule[0]["repetition"])
    block = []
    for row in schedule:
        if (row["task_id"], row["repetition"]) != identity:
            break
        block.append(row)
    arms = [arm["arm_id"] for arm in freeze["arms"]]
    require(len(block) == len(arms) and len(set(arms)) == len(arms) and
            {row["arm_id"] for row in block} == set(arms),
            "first block must contain every admitted arm exactly once")
    return block


def _file_inventory(root: Path) -> list[dict]:
    """Hash and conservatively scan every retained regular artifact."""
    root = root.absolute()
    require(root.is_dir() and root.resolve() == root and not root.is_symlink(),
            "canonical first-block artifact directory required")
    inventory = []
    for directory, directories, files in os.walk(root, followlinks=False):
        directories.sort()
        files.sort()
        for name in [*directories, *files]:
            path = Path(directory) / name
            if path.parent == root and name in {AUDIT_NAME, DECISION_NAME}:
                continue
            info = path.lstat()
            require(not stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode), "artifact tree contains a symlink")
            if stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode):
                continue
            require(stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) and info.st_nlink == 1,
                    "artifact evidence must be a unique regular file")
            observed = 0
            hasher = hashlib.sha256()
            tail = ""
            with path.open("rb") as stream:
                while chunk := stream.read(1024 * 1024):
                    observed += len(chunk)
                    hasher.update(chunk)
                    text = tail + chunk.decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
                    require(not any(pattern.search(text) for pattern in SECRET_PATTERNS),
                            "secret scan rejected retained first-block evidence")
                    tail = text[-4096:]
            relative = str(path.relative_to(root))
            inventory.append({"path": relative, "bytes": observed,

    return inventory

    """Verify the sibling task-input store; None means the historical in-root layout."""
    from agent_harness_evals.task_input_store import verify_store
    bindings = {task["task_id"]: task["archive_binding"]
                for task in freeze.get("corpus", {}).get("tasks", []) if "archive_binding" in task}
    return verify_store(Path(artifact_root), bindings, configuration.get("archive_roots", {}))

    """Reservation precedes admission; the launcher writes intent afterward."""
    try:
        reserved, launched, finished = (
            datetime.fromisoformat(value) for value in (
                attempt.get("started_at"), intent.get("started_at"), attempt.get("finished_at")))
        return (all(value.utcoffset() is not None for value in (reserved, launched, finished))
                and reserved <= launched <= finished)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return False

    in the final inventory. Any native evidence in the old directory disallows it.
    """
    original_root = artifact_root / lease_id
    name = f"prelaunch-recovery-{lease_id}.json"

    recovery = read_local(artifact_root, name)
    require(recovery.get("schema_version") == "stage-a-prelaunch-recovery/1" and
            recovery.get("lease_id") == lease_id and

            recovery.get("configuration_digest") == configuration_digest and

            "prelaunch recovery differs from the frozen execution")
    require(recovery.get("resumed_directory") == f"{lease_id}-prelaunch-resume-r1",

            interrupted.get("lease_id") == lease_id and interrupted.get("error_type") == "ValueError" and

    freeze: Mapping,
    state: Mapping,
    *,
    artifact_root: Path,
    configuration_digest: str,
    resource_state: Mapping,
    sealed_at: str,
) -> dict:
    """Rebuild the all-scheduled Stage A accounting without inventing results."""
    require(
        freeze.get("purpose") == "freeze"
        and freeze.get("stage") == "stage_a"
        and freeze.get("schema_version") == "staged-multilang-benchmark/5",
        "execution seal requires the final seven-arm Stage A freeze",
    )
    validate_frozen_outcome_contract(
        freeze["outcome_contract"], freeze["outcome_slot_plan"]
    )
    require(
        state.get("manifest_digest") == digest(freeze)
        and state.get("manifest_purpose") == "freeze"
        and state.get("stage") == "stage_a",
        "scheduler ledger belongs to another manifest or stage",
    )
    require(
        not state.get("reservations")
        and not any(slot.get("status") in {"pending", "in_flight"} for slot in state["slots"]),
        "every scheduled slot must be terminal or explicitly unstarted",
    )
    require(dict(resource_state) == QUIESCENT_RESOURCES, "execution resources are not quiescent")

    rows = []
    for slot in state["slots"]:
        if slot["status"] == "unstarted":
            rows.append(_unstarted_row(slot))
        else:
            rows.append(
                _attempt_row(
                    freeze, slot, Path(artifact_root), configuration_digest
                )
            )
    records = [row["task_outcome_v2"] for row in rows if row["task_outcome_v2"]]
    for row in rows:
        outcome = row["task_outcome_v2"]
        primary = outcome["outcome_dimensions"]["primary_task_outcome"] if outcome else None
        disposition = row["disposition"]
        row.update(
            scheduled=True,
            attempted=row["attempt_id"] is not None,
            valid=bool(primary and primary["denominator"] == "capability"),
            unsupported=disposition == "unsupported",
            infrastructure_missing=bool(
                disposition in {"infrastructure_missing", "infrastructure_failed"}
                or (primary and primary["denominator"] == "infrastructure_missing")
            ),
            unstarted=disposition == "unstarted",
        )
    dimensions = (
        "scheduled",
        "attempted",
        "valid",
        "unsupported",
        "infrastructure_missing",
        "unstarted",
    )
    task_outcome_seal = None
    if len(records) == len(rows):
        roots = {
            row["slot_id"]: Path(artifact_root) / row["lease_id"] for row in rows
        }
        task_outcome_seal = _build_partitioned_outcome_seal(
            stage_id=freeze["outcome_slot_plan"]["stage_id"],
            sealed_at=sealed_at,
            records=records,
            frozen_slot_plan=freeze["outcome_slot_plan"],
            frozen_outcome_contract=freeze["outcome_contract"],
            artifact_roots=roots,
        )
    return {
        "schema_version": SCHEMA,
        "stage_id": "stage-a",
        "sealed_at": sealed_at,
        "manifest_digest": digest(freeze),
        "slot_plan_digest": digest(freeze["outcome_slot_plan"]),
        "outcome_contract_digest": digest(freeze["outcome_contract"]),
        "scheduler_state_digest": digest(state),
        "configuration_digest": configuration_digest,
        "resource_state": dict(resource_state),
        "denominators": {name: sum(bool(row[name]) for row in rows) for name in dimensions},
        "slots": rows,
        "records": records,
        # The v2 outcome seal requires one terminal task record for every slot.
        # Unstarted slots intentionally have no task-bearing record and remain
        # sealed by the outer all-scheduled execution record instead.
        "task_outcome_seal": task_outcome_seal,
    }

# Proposal: recover an interrupted Stage A reservation without replay

Status: implementation plan only; **not** an operator authorization. The current
[continuous-cohort runbook](../runbooks/stage-a-continuous-cohort.md#stop-and-resume)
still stops on an uncertain reservation. Do not apply this procedure to a live
ledger until its implementation, admission and owner review are complete.

## Existing boundary

- The `archive-stage-a-cohort/1` freeze is published from the exact owner-approved
  candidate, admission and host digest; publication writes the gate before the
  configured freeze and has a checksum-checked, no-overwrite recovery for that
  gap. The ledger is initialized once from that freeze. `verify_plan`,
  `verify_configured_freeze` and `load_state` reject a changed approval,
  configuration, plan or manifest digest. The 23 ordered prepared-archive tasks,
  seven standard arms, one attempt per slot and 161 schedule/slot-plan entries
  remain fixed; no first-block stop is inserted. See the [publication and init
  steps](../runbooks/stage-a-continuous-cohort.md#10-publish-the-approved-freeze),
  [scheduler contract](../runbooks/stage-aware-scheduler.md#frozen-inputs) and
  [numerical reconciliation](../runbooks/seven-arm-stage-a-freeze.md).
- `stage_a_launcher.run_block` rehearses before reservation; `dispatch_next`
  then persists an `in_flight` slot and account reservation, *before* creating
  `<lease>/intent.json`. `execute_attempt` runs native work, confirms cleanup,
  verifies independently, normalizes a result and returns a completion;
  launcher writes `completion.json`, then calls `record_attempt` under the
  ledger lock. An exception writes `interrupted.json` but does not release the
  reservation. A kill may precede either file. A stopped unit with no
  reservation may be restarted; with a reservation `run_block` refuses to run.
- `run_cohort_step` validates chained clean-block progress, catches up a block
  settled in the ledger but missing its progress record, and never advances
  over an active lease. The offline cohort audit validates the whole checkpoint,
  progress, artifacts and research evidence; the execution seal requires that
  exact passing audit, quiescent resources and one row per scheduled slot.
  `_attempt_row` currently requires a real completion, normalized result and
  lifecycle for **every attempted terminal slot**. A missing result cannot be
  passed off as `unstarted`: that disposition requires no attempt. The v2
  task-outcome seal is emitted only if all scheduled slots have task records;
  the outer execution seal accounts for missing records. See
  `stage_a_first_block.py`, `stage_a_cohort_audit.py`, `stage_a_seal.py`.
- [Scoped Inspect recovery](../runbooks/inspect-recovery-and-shakedown.md#operator-recovery)
  proves abandoned ownership and cleans only linked resources; it does not
  decide an outcome or refund charges. The narrow [prelaunch Claude
  recovery](../runbooks/stage-a-first-block-gate.md) requires proof that *no*
  native execution began and is not a general host-interruption precedent.

## Decision and state machine

Choose **evidence-based terminal reconciliation** for a genuinely interrupted
native attempt, not replay or process continuation. Recovery is an explicit
owner-authorized action on the *existing lease* after the unit is stopped. No
new dispatch, attempt number, native call, grader run or provider request.

| Observed state after a stop | Action | Next state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No lease, pending slot | Fix pre-reservation cause and restart same unit; after window end reconcile pending as unstarted. | pending → in_flight on ordinary dispatch, or pending → unstarted after end |
| No lease, block settled but progress missing | Existing checked-ledger catch-up. | terminal slots unchanged; append progress |
| Active lease, `completion.json` already durable but ledger finish missing | Verify intent, result, evidence, cleanup, account journal and completion exactly as the audit would; under locks finish that same lease with its original typed disposition/digest, then append progress if block settled. Do **not** execute worker. | in_flight → terminal |
| Active lease, no valid completion, native possibly started | Prove owner abandoned and all native/Inspect/verifier/research resources quiescent; retain partial artifacts and charged usage. With explicit owner decision and recovery attestation, finish the same lease as `infrastructure_failed` with a *new nonretryable* `host_interrupted` error code and an explicit missing-result recovery receipt. | in_flight → terminal (no task score) |
| Active lease, ownership or accounting uncertain, unexpected/contradictory evidence, or cleanup fails | Stop. No ledger mutation or block advancement; escalate to owner, possibly retire the *entire* attempt under the existing runbook. | in_flight unchanged |

Replay would risk a second provider charge or different patch under the same
frozen slot; a second attempt violates the one-attempt limit. Continuing a
partly streamed native process after reboot cannot prove original sandbox,
credentials, time budget or isolation and must not be implemented. Finishing
from already sealed completion evidence is **recording recovery**, not native
resume. The earlier Claude no-native-work exception remains separate and
must not silently become permission to retry an uncertain native call. An
interruption is infrastructure missing, never an incorrect patch, unsupported
task, zero score or an unstarted slot. Other six arms and remaining task blocks
stay scheduled in their original order.

## Implementation slices (test first at each seam)

1. Add a *read-only* recovery inspection command on the admitted checkout,
   holding the launcher lock then the scheduler lock in the existing order.
   Authenticate published freeze/approval/plan/slot plan, configuration, host
   profile, target admission, ledger event history, exact lease/slot/attempt
   identity and progress prefix. Inventory `intent`, `interrupted`, `completion`,
   native/verification artifacts and task-input store without following links.
   Classify only the states above; do not infer "never started" from a missing
   file. Record a digest of the pre-recovery scheduler checkpoint. Reject a
   second running launcher, changed execution commit or stale admission rather
   than rebind to a new freeze. Keep diagnostics credential-free.
2. Implement a bounded, scoped quiescence check using Inspect ownership
   receipts, Docker endpoint/member labels, owner PID/start/boot identity and
   `recover_abandoned_trials` where applicable; confirm no surviving native
   process, verifier, credential consumer or research service and verify the
   image/store state. Re-export volatile leases only for *future* slots. Never
   perform a global Docker sweep. Reconcile the conserved research journal's
   per-trial charges and active reservations against the original trial, without
   deleting/refunding rows; the existing live-remainder gate still applies to
   all unsettled future slots. If receipts or accounting cannot prove safety,
   leave the lease active.
3. Introduce a versioned, immutable recovery attestation under the canonical
   artifact root, binding freeze and outcome-slot-plan digests, configuration,
   admitted execution commit, checkpoint digest, lease/attempt/trial, original
   artifact inventory, cleanup receipts, charged-use snapshot, timestamps,
   owner identity/decision and reason. Persist it no-replace and hash it in a
   distinct recovery completion. Recheck all inputs while holding the same
   locks immediately before `record_attempt`; if a crash occurs before the
   ledger update, rerunning must verify and reuse the same attestation, not
   manufacture a second one. If a crash occurs after the ledger update, verify
   terminal digest and treat as done. An existing ordinary completion must take
   the recording-only branch and never be overwritten.
4. Add a narrowly gated scheduler transition via existing `record_attempt` for
   the same lease, with `infrastructure_failed` / `host_interrupted`, no retry
   eligibility and full frozen account consumption. Do not broaden `reconcile_pending`
   (which forbids in-flight work), reset a reservation, edit `limits`, change
   schedule/order, or permit a second dispatch. Validate the new code against
   the frozen retry policy: if policy/schema interpretation needs changing,
   implement as a backward-compatible *evidence interpretation* for this
   terminal recovery, not a mutation of the approved freeze. Historical
   ledgers remain validated with their recorded implementation.
5. Teach the cohort audit and outer execution seal a distinct **attempted,
   interrupted, no-result** row, requiring the attestation and recovery
   completion hash to equal scheduler terminal evidence; validate original
   artifacts/inventory, account charges, quiescence and absence of a scored
   result. Count it as attempted and infrastructure missing, not valid or
   unstarted. Do not synthesize `result.json`/`lifecycle.json` or a v2 task
   outcome. The outer seal includes all 161 slots and may have a null v2
   task-outcome seal (as with unstarted slots). Downstream Stage B admission
   must not treat this as a solved or failed capability task; require explicit
   owner disposition for any incomplete comparative screen. Preserve all seven
   arm IDs and planned slots in every report.
6. Update the continuous-cohort stop/resume and audit/seal runbooks *after*
   validation: owner confirmation, exact command/expected receipt, failure
   cases, research and resource evidence retention. Add a dry-run inspection
   first and prohibit automatic invocation by the systemd restart loop.

## Acceptance tests and rollback

Use fixture freezes at the scheduler seam, then an archive-cohort fixture with
23 × 7 slots at the launcher/audit/seal seams. Red before green: reservation
before intent, kill during native, kill after native cleanup but before
verification, complete artifact before ledger finish, kill before/after
attestation and after ledger finish, settled block before progress. Assert no
second native call, no second lease, no refund, unchanged frozen digests and
order, correct charged-work remainder and exactly one progress record. Reject
live owner/PID reuse or unverified boot, mixed Docker labels, missing cleanup,
changed approval/slot plan/commit, symlink or altered artifact, stale checkpoint,
forged completion and missing owner decision. Test no-score seal counts and
Stage B refusal separately; test a restart of an ordinary pending slot and
finite-window reconciliation unchanged. Run focused scheduler, launcher,
Inspect recovery, numerical, cohort audit, seal and Stage B consumer tests;
reserve `make check` for final integrated acceptance.

Before rollout, keep the old fail-closed binary/runbook as the rollback path.
If any new check fails, stop the unit and retain ledger, artifacts, task-input
store, research journal and ownership receipts untouched. Before a terminal
transition one may revert code and remain stopped; after it, **never** roll the
ledger back or resume under older code that cannot interpret the new evidence.
Pin the new revision and audit/seal there, or retire the whole attempt with
owner approval, retaining all prior evidence and starting a separately
approved freeze/ledger. A code revision or new cohort is not an in-place
change to the approved 23-task, seven-arm freeze.
